Caption: Fig. 1. Representative acquisition conditions and reference FDI annotations. Panoramic radiographs, smartphone intraoral photographs, and DSLR photographs are shown with their existing bounding-box annotations. The examples illustrate differences in global field of view, tooth scale, framing, and illumination. Visible spaces alone do not establish clinically missing teeth.

Fig. 2. Shared detector and acquisition-specific components. CMFA replaces four adjacent-scale fusion sites for Mobile/DSLR; HOOA refines Mobile feature levels. Factor heads provide supervision for Mobile/Pano and score fusion only for Mobile. Their quadrant, position, and dentition fusion weights are 0.10, 0.05, and 0.03. The K-class, four-prototype-per-class bank supplies auxiliary training supervision only. Pano uses fixed training-derived center and shape scores, while DSLR uses DualOpt during optimization. The dataset label map decodes outputs into clinical FDI codes. Solid arrows denote prediction flow; dashed arrows denote auxiliary supervision or prior fitting. Component roles are summarized in Table 2.

Fig. 3. Training-derived center templates for the 32 permanent DENTEX FDI classes. Each panel shows the class-specific center distribution in normalized image coordinates, based on training-box means and full regularized covariances. The templates are fixed at inference and are separate from the learnable appearance prototypes; shape statistics are provided in Supplementary Fig. S1.

Fig. 4. Cross-scale mutual feature aggregation (CMFA). Spatially aligned inputs A and B have equal projected width C = 256. (A) Their concatenation supplies a global-average-pooling and two-layer pointwise channel gate, which is split into gA and gB. (B) The gated inputs are exchanged through A + B ⊙ gB and B + A ⊙ gA, then concatenated. (C) Channel mean and maximum statistics of the concatenated feature produce a 7 × 7 sigmoid spatial gate. The output retains 2C = 512 channels. Cat denotes channel concatenation; circular multiplication and addition nodes operate elementwise.

Fig. 5. High-order omni-attention (HOOA). (A) Local and dilated-context branches generate L and C; the high-pass input X − AvgPool₃(X) supplies an edge branch E. The second-order response L ⊙ sigmoid(C) is concatenated with L and E and projected to F. (B) Channel and spatial gates are both computed from F before gating. Their product modulates F, and the update is added to X with bounded scale α = 0.30 sigmoid(s). DW and PW denote depthwise and pointwise convolutions. Local and edge convolutions include batch normalization and SiLU; the context branch uses SiLU after its depthwise convolution and batch normalization after its final pointwise convolution. Spatial statistics are channel-wise mean and maximum. Tensor glyphs illustrate feature shape, not measured response maps.

Fig. 6. Three-seed performance of the acquisition-specific configurations. Small circles show the actual outcomes for seeds 0, 1, and 2; larger markers and bars show mean ± sample SD. Each cohort has its own labelled AP axis. Pano includes combined center–shape scoring. No between-model improvement or statistical superiority is inferred from these within-configuration error bars.

Fig. 7. Mobile framework-level AP comparison. Labels identify each detector and its AP. Error bars show sample SD only for the three-seed DENT-STRIDE-Mobile, official DEIM-s, and RT-DETRv2-S entries; other methods are single-seed observations. Input resolution, pretraining, and native training/output settings differ across frameworks, as specified in Section 4.6. The plot describes system performance rather than an isolated identity-module effect.

Fig. 8. HOOA branch comparison on the same smartphone images. Independently trained seed-0 models retain the same training protocol and differ only in the high-pass and second-order branches. Columns show the original image, ground truth, three branch-removal configurations, and full HOOA; lower rows show identical target enlargements. Teal boxes are ground truth and orange boxes are predictions retained at score ≥0.30. (A) The highlighted reference tooth is FDI 41; No high-pass: FDI 42, 14 correct matches and 7 false positives; No second-order: FDI 42, 14 correct matches and 10 false positives; Neither branch: FDI 42, 10 correct matches and 15 false positives; Full HOOA: FDI 41, 16 correct matches and 7 false positives. (B) The highlighted reference tooth is FDI 81; No high-pass: FDI 41, 10 correct matches and 9 false positives; No second-order: FDI 41, 10 correct matches and 5 false positives; Neither branch: FDI 41, 11 correct matches and 10 false positives; Full HOOA: FDI 81, 13 correct matches and 6 false positives. These selected examples illustrate branch effects; the complete validation ablation determines their aggregate AP differences.

Fig. 9. Four-way anatomical scoring at identical Pano weights. (A) AP and (B) AR100. Small circles show the actual outcomes of the three seed-specific checkpoints under no prior, center, shape, and combined scoring. Larger markers and bars show mean ± sample SD. All scores are recomputed before native top-k selection; weights and predicted box coordinates are unchanged.

Fig. 10. Same-weight DENTEX anatomical-prior comparison. The same seed-2 checkpoint is evaluated without a prior, with center scoring, with shape scoring, and with both. Scores are recomputed from all ordinary query–class candidates before native top-k selection; box coordinates do not change. Original images and reference annotations are accompanied by identical target enlargements. Teal boxes denote ground truth and orange boxes predictions retained at score ≥0.30. (A) At the same query box, the highest retained label changes from FDI 46 to FDI 45 for reference FDI 45; image-level correct matches change from 19 to 20. (B) At the same query box, the highest retained label changes from FDI 47 to FDI 48 for reference FDI 47; image-level correct matches change from 25 to 24. The favorable and adverse examples illustrate score-ranking effects rather than a change in learned localization.

Fig. 11. Retrained HOOA and factor-supervision ablations. Bars report AP differences after each branch or supervision-target removal. HOOA uses the full Mobile seed-0 configuration (54.910 AP); factor supervision uses all three targets with training and inference fusion disabled (55.537 AP). Every tested removal is shown. These single-seed results have no uncertainty bars.

Fig. 13. Actual CMFA/HOOA forward-pass responses for the same Mobile image shown in Fig. 8A. CMFA channel gates gA/gB are arranged as 16 × 16 channel-index grids; Gs is the spatial gate. HOOA panels show local, context, high-pass, second-order, channel/spatial gates, input, and output. Sigmoid gates use their actual [0,1] values. Response RMS maps are divided by their respective 99th percentile and clipped to [0,1]. These are native internal tensors, not Grad-CAM or causal evidence from visualization alone.

Fig. S1. Normalized width and height distributions of the 16,234 DENTEX training boxes, grouped by the 32 permanent FDI classes. The distributions describe training geometry; the SpatialShape shape term uses the joint regularized quadratic score of log-width and log-height. No validation boxes are used to fit these templates.

Fig. S2. Complete component-sensitivity plots for settings not emphasized in main Fig. 11. All displayed points are seed-0 observations, without uncertainty bars. ΔAP uses the group-specific reference in Table S2 or the factor-fusion-off reference in Table S5. Positive values indicate an alternative that exceeds the reference; they are not gains attributed to the intact module.

Fig. S3. Same-checkpoint center, shape, and combined prior effects. Points show the mean paired AP difference versus no prior and bars show exploratory Student-t 95% intervals over the three seeds (df = 2). The zero line denotes no AP change. Intervals are conditional on validation-selected weights and are not patient-sampling or independent-test intervals.

Fig. S4. Detection and threshold diagnostics for the final seed-0 configurations. Rows show Pano, Mobile, and DSLR. Columns show category-macro-averaged COCO interpolated precision at IoU 0.50 and maxDets = 100, F1, and raw duplicate-image rate. Unsupported categories are omitted from the precision average. Thresholds range from 0.05 to 0.95 in steps of 0.05; dotted lines indicate 0.30. These are cohort-level detection diagnostics, not clinical charting-error estimates.

Fig. S5. Complete Pano FDI outcome matrix and class support for the final seed-0 configuration. Gray rows have no validation support and are unavailable, not zero-accuracy classes.
